new: This links development economics with behavioural economics and choice architecture. In the IB course, choice architecture and nudges are HL only (2.4 and 2.7).

old: Friedman and others argued that fiscal policy acts with long and variable lags
new: Friedman and others argued that discretionary policy, monetary as well as fiscal, acts with long and variable lags
why: Friedman’s ‘long and variable lags’ phrase was made about monetary policy, so tying it to fiscal policy alone misattributes it.

old: based on information problems rather than rigid wages.
new: in which wages stay above the market-clearing level because of information problems, not because of minimum wages or union bargaining.
why: Efficiency wages are themselves a source of real-wage rigidity, so contrasting them with ‘rigid wages’ mischaracterises the model.

old: The familiar diagram, with price on the vertical axis and an equilibrium where the curves cross, is largely his.
new: Earlier writers such as Cournot and Fleeming Jenkin had drawn demand and supply curves, but Marshall’s version, with price on the vertical axis and an equilibrium where the curves cross, is the one that became standard.
why: Demand and supply curves predate Marshall (Cournot 1838, Jenkin 1870); he popularised rather than originated the diagram.
